projection_invariants: Every nonterminal execution has exactly one primary ownership projection: C or B, except an explicit CONTROL_LOST hold awaiting disposition.
C and B are mutually exclusive for one execution.
M is a per-session read-only subscription and may coexist with C or B.
At most one active controller lease exists per execution control domain.
A monitor never gains prompt, command, edit, breakpoint, action, schedule, or lease authority from its M projection.
Background mode is an explicit committed transition and is never inferred from disconnect or lease loss.

background_rules: Opening directly in B requires BackgroundAllowed and Automatic true; otherwise reject or create PAUSED awaiting explicit control according to the request.
B may continue deterministic simulator work and durable waits without a browser.
When B reaches a prompt or another interactive decision, it enters SUSPENDED with hold_reason CONTROL_LOST, raises a durable warning, and waits for authenticated acquisition.
B cannot synthesize prompt defaults solely because no controller exists; only the prompt's pinned timeout policy may settle it.
Taking control from B creates a new lease and fence; it does not rewrite prior B history.
disconnect_restart_rules: Browser disconnect alone does not instantly transfer control or select B.
The active lease remains authoritative until a committed release, expiry, revocation, or handover.
On lease loss, execution pauses at a safe point and preserves its saved resume target.
Restart reconstructs the current lease by ControllerLeaseId, revision, fence, and database deadline; it creates no implicit holder.
Authenticated reacquisition acknowledges active executions, prompts, alarms, and uncertain effects, then allocates a new or policy-valid renewed authority before explicit resume.
strict_monitor_denials: control acquisition when an active lease exists
